original_question: Derive non-trivial lower or upper bounds for distinct distances determined by points constrained to algebraic varieties in R^d for dimensions d >= 3.
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 14: the deliberately vague higher-dimensional restricted-variety distinct-distances problem that follows the discussion of points on constant-degree curves in ℝ^d and on constant-degree algebraic surfaces in ℝ^3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's higher-dimensional distinct-distances problem for points lying on varieties in real Euclidean space, and it keeps the key scope d ≥ 3 that appears in the paper's official problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
missing_details: It should specify that the object of study is a single finite set P of n points contained in one variety V ⊂ ℝ^d, and that one counts the distinct Euclidean distances determined by unordered pairs from P; otherwise the question is not stand-alone.

It should make explicit that this is the non-bipartite version. The paper treats the two-set/bipartite higher-dimensional variant separately later as Problem 21, so that ambiguity should be removed. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
It should define what 'distinct distances' means, for example D(P) := |{|p-q| : p,q ∈ P, p ≠ q}|.

It should note that Problem 14 is intentionally broad: the paper does not ask for an exact asymptotic formula, does not fix a single exponent, and does not specify whether one seeks lower bounds, upper constructions, or both; it only asks for non-trivial bounds. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

It should acknowledge the nearby context: the motivating known case is points on a constant-degree algebraic surface in ℝ^3, where the paper asks whether exclusions such as planes and spheres are really necessary. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

It should clarify that the dimension of the variety itself is not fixed by Problem 14; the surrounding discussion explicitly broadens from curves to surfaces to algebraic varieties of any dimension. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
It should state the asymptotic quantifier explicitly, e.g. 'for n sufficiently large' or 'as n → ∞'.
It should keep the ambient field/metric explicit: real Euclidean space ℝ^d with ordinary Euclidean distance.
refined_question: For each fixed integer d ≥ 3, let V ⊂ ℝ^d be an algebraic variety and let P ⊂ V be a finite set of n points. Define D(P) := |{|p-q| : p,q ∈ P, p ≠ q}|, the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by pairs of points of P. Derive asymptotically non-trivial bounds for D(P) as n → ∞ for point sets constrained to such varieties, and determine which geometric restrictions on V (for example, whether exceptional cases analogous to planes or spheres must be excluded in the surface case) are needed to guarantee such bounds. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at Section 4's closing open problem, not at the planar restricted-set questions and not at the later bipartite problem. The decisive verbal match is the request for 'non-trivial' bounds for points on varieties in ℝ^d with d ≥ 3; the paper introduces this immediately after discussing the curve case (Problem 13) and the known surface case in ℝ^3, and explicitly says it is 'a deliberately vague problem.' I therefore kept the reformulation narrow, single-set, and higher-dimensional, while making only the minimal hidden definitions explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
